transcript.content: Hello, it's nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Nice to meet you too, doctor. Well, I guess I'm here because of my eating. 

After my late shifts, I'll stop for takeout on the way home, and I usually end up eating... well, two whole burgers, a large fries, and a shake. But then I still go home and just clean out whatever leftovers are in the garage fridge. It's honestly like I'm having a whole second supper right after the first one. I just feel like it's getting out of hand and I need to figure out what's going on.
When you eat this way, do you feel unable to stop or control how much you’re eating?

Yeah, that's exactly what happens. Once I start, it just feels like a switch gets flipped. I'll literally be sitting there telling myself, 'Roy, shut the bag and go inside,' but... my hands just keep reaching for more. I really do feel like I can't stop it once I get going.
How often do episodes like this happen?

Well, for the past few months, it's been... usually at least one night a week. But honestly, it's often two or three times a week. It mostly happens after I pull a late shift, or just... if I've had a really rough day on the line.
After these episodes, do you do anything to try to make up for the eating, such as vomiting, fasting, or exercising excessively?

No, I don't do any of that. I just... I usually just feel really full and kind of disgusted with myself, so I'll just go to sleep. I don't throw up or skip meals the next day or go run it off or anything. I just wake up the next morning and go to work like normal.
